{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Joel Alan Smoller''' (2 January 1936 – 27 September 2017) was an American mathematician.

Joel Smoller was born in [[Brooklyn]] on 2 January 1936 to parents Benjamin, a taxicab driver, and Olga, who died when he was young.<ref name="michrec">{{cite news |title=Obituary: Joel Smoller |url=https://record.umich.edu/articles/obituary-joel-smoller-0 |accessdate=14 April 2019 |work=The University Record |publisher=University of Michigan |date=13 November 2017}}</ref><ref name="annobit">{{cite news |title=Joel Smoller |url=http://obits.mlive.com/obituaries/annarbor/obituary.aspx?n=joel-smoller&pid=186796275 |accessdate=14 April 2019 |work=Ann Arbor News |date=1 October 2017}}</ref> Smoller attended [[New York University]], and completed his doctoral work at [[Purdue University]] in 1963, after which he taught at the University of Michigan. In 1970, he was appointed a full professor, and assumed the [[Lamberto Cesari]] Collegiate Professorship of Mathematics in 1998.<ref name="michrec"/><ref name="annobit"/> He was editor of ''[[Transactions of the American Mathematical Society]]'' from 1981 to 1985, and later the ''Journal for Applicable Analysis''.<ref>{{cite news |title=Past lecturers: Joel Smoller |url=http://patten.indiana.edu/lecturers2/Smoller-Joel.html |accessdate=14 April 2019 |publisher=Indiana University Bloomington}}</ref> Smoller was award a [[Guggenheim Fellowship]] in 1979,<ref>{{cite news |title=Joel A. Smollet |url=https://www.gf.org/fellows/all-fellows/joel-a-smoller/ |accessdate=14 April 2019 |publisher=John Simon Guggenheim Memorial Foundation}}</ref> the [[George David Birkhoff Prize]] in 2009,<ref name="michrec"/> and elected to fellowship of the [[American Mathematical Society]] in 2013, a member of its inaugural class of fellows.<ref>{{cite news |title=List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society |url=http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |accessdate=14 April 2019 |publisher=American Mathematical Society}}</ref> Smoller retired in June 2017, and died, aged 81, on 27 September 2017.<ref name="michrec"/><ref name="annobit"/> Following his death, the Joel Smoller Graduate Fellowship was established.<ref>{{cite news |title=Joel Smoller, 1936-2017 |url=https://lsa.umich.edu/math/news-events/all-news/search-news/joel-smoller--1936-2017.html |accessdate=14 April 2019 |publisher=University of Michigan |date=2017}}</ref>
